# The Anchor

Geir Ketilson (D-0132). The third member of the pseudo-family: its bedrock and its
bite. ("Anchor" remains a working role label, not an in-world title.)

## The ratified shape

> status: ratified (D-0050, D-0063, D-0096)

Explicitly not another woman: he IS male (settled by D-0096 — "anchor is male") —
older, handicapped, with a bit of tragic backstory, directions the author flagged as
wanting more thought. He
and the protagonist share a real history that predates the story's opening (D-0062),
and there is no romance between them whatsoever: he may be gay, or simply old and
past interest — unsettled — but he is certainly not romantically interested in the
protagonist. In hostile territory the trio passes as a family — a couple and their
daughter (or son, as the day requires) — a cover, never a truth.

## Working role

> status: provisional (D-0072)

The session's model: the physical intelligence of the party. A former heavy laborer
of the extraction economy — broken by it and expert in it — he handles iron, repair,
loads, perimeters, weather, and the brutal practicalities the other two are
constitutionally bad at. He is the embodiment of criminalized competence: the
right-to-repair underground in one scarred body ([[economy]], [[professions]]). His
register: dry, cynical, Mr-Bennet-sidelong; the working-class check on the
protagonist's abstractions and the apprentice's improvisations.

## Origin

> status: provisional (D-0080, D-0081)

From the industrial crags ([[regions]]): mine-country, where the body is the tool and
the bill always comes. His disability and his lungs are receipts, not metaphors.

## Backstory

> status: ratified (D-0115)

He is the protagonist's extraction, made flesh (D-0115): as an imperial calculator she was
once sent to "resolve" a crag mine's Wyrd-debt, and her arithmetic condemned it — a collapse
that took his lungs (or a leg) and killed others. He is the living receipt of her worst
imperial act; their partnership is penance and slow forgiveness, played cold and revealed
late, never as spectacle (D-0076). On the ghost the protagonist carries: he suspects.
He has watched her "become" someone else in a fugue and drawn his own conclusions, but decency
and Frith keep him silent until it matters — the Mr-Bennet read, a dry man who knows more than
he lets on. (The higher-drama alternative — that he has always known, and has deliberately kept
the apprentice's greatest secret — is held in reserve.) His disability, his lungs, and his
sexuality remain his own to fill in; the no-romance rule with the protagonist stands (D-0063).

## The unseen finish (his gift)

> status: ratified (D-0123)

The forbidden, economically useless thing he secretly teaches the apprentice is the perfect
unseen finish (D-0123): how to forge or tie a thing to a standard no one will ever see — the
hidden dovetail, the maker's-mark inside the joint, the back of the work made beautiful. It is
the exact inversion of keep-stamped shoddiness (a licensed tool *must* be shoddy, so making one
beautiful is contraband pride): joy as craft-dignity, the thing the Ledger cannot measure
(D-0087). The lesson deliberately crosses the craft-cultures: the crag-iron man teaches the
fringe knot-child a joy that lives in iron, a craft-culture away from their own knots. The
warmer, audible variant — a useless reed or bone whistle — is kept in reserve. See [[economy]] on keep-stamped
shoddiness and [[apprentice]] on their knot-craft.
